title: ValueError: blake2b blocked on FIPS systems since 1.57.0
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit 1.57.0 raises ValueError on FIPS-compliant Python environments (any system running Python against an OpenSSL in FIPS mode). The app fails to perform any hashing operation — element ID generation, cache key computation, file watching all break. Streamlit 1.56.0 is unaffected.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit.util import create_fast_hasher

h = create_fast_hasher()
h.update(b"hello")
print(h.hexdigest())
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run this on any FIPS-enforcing Python 3.x environment (e.g. a Chainguard python-fips image, RHEL 9 with FIPS mode enabled, or any OpenSSL built with enable-fips).

### Expected Behavior

Streamlit starts and runs normally. blake2b is used for non-security purposes (element IDs, cache keys, file change detection) and should be callable on FIPS systems with `usedforsecurity=False`.

### Current Behavior

Any code path that calls create_fast_hasher() or calc_hash() raises ValueError and crashes.

```python
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test_hashing.py", line 3, in <module>
    h = create_fast_hasher()
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../site-packages/streamlit/util.py", line 74, in create_fast_hasher
    return hashlib.blake2b(digest_size=16)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/usr/lib/python3.12/hashlib.py", line 86, in __usedforsecurity_check
    raise ValueError(name + " is blocked when usedforsecurity=True")
ValueError: blake2b is blocked when usedforsecurity=True
```

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

Streamlit: 1.57.0 (regression; 1.56.0 works)
Python: 3.12 (reproduced; also expected on 3.10, 3.11)


### Additional Information

Introduced by: #14842 — which replaced MD5 with blake2b but omitted usedforsecurity=False

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15148)

Confirmed regression in Streamlit 1.57.0 on FIPS-enforcing Python environments (e.g. RHEL 9 with FIPS mode, Chainguard `python-fips`). PR [#14842](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/14842) replaced the previous MD5-based fast hasher with `hashlib.blake2b(digest_size=16)` in `create_fast_hasher` (`lib/streamlit/util.py:74`) but did not pass `usedforsecurity=False`. On a FIPS-restricted OpenSSL, `blake2b` is blocked by default and raises `ValueError: blake2b is blocked when usedforsecurity=True`, breaking every code path that uses `create_fast_hasher()` / `calc_hash()` — element ID generation, cache key computation, file-watcher hashing, fragment IDs, etc. The previous MD5 implementation correctly passed `usedforsecurity=False` (added in PR [#10413](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/10413) to fix [#10412](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10412)), so this is effectively a reintroduction of the same class of FIPS bug. The fix is a one-line change: `hashlib.blake2b(digest_size=16, usedforsecurity=False)` (and a regression test that exercises FIPS-style enforcement).

### Related Issues

- [#10412](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10412) — Streamlit fragment feature broke on a FIPS-compliant python image (same failure mode, fixed previously by adding `usedforsecurity=False` to MD5 calls).
- [#7120](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7120) — Original FIPS compliance request that introduced the `usedforsecurity=False` pattern across `forward_msg_cache.py` and `watcher/util.py`; the same pattern needs to be re-applied to the new blake2b hasher.
- [#7526](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7526) — "Making streamlit FIPS compliant" — broader FIPS compliance tracking issue; this regression undoes part of that effort.
